title: What If a Full-Scale Nuclear War Blocked the Sun?

scenes.text: What if a nuclear war happened? The blasts are not the biggest problem. The sky is.
Burning cities would lift soot into the stratosphere. A 2022 study found more than five teragrams is enough to cause mass food shortages.
Soot would dim sunlight and cool the planet, so crops get less light and less warmth.
In the largest war scenario, global calorie production falls about ninety percent, three to four years after the fighting.
More than seventy-five percent of the world's people would be starving within two years.
Researchers estimate over five billion could die of hunger. Even the smallest regional war cut calories by about seven percent.

description:
What if a full-scale nuclear war happened?
A 2022 Nature Food study modeled soot blocking sunlight and found global crop calories could fall about 90 percent.
